title: Node.js Core Modules Quick Revision: fs, path, http, os, URL
summary: Night-before revision notes on Node's core modules: the three fs API styles, path.join vs path.resolve, __dirname in ES modules, a minimal http server, os and process info, and URL parsing. Ends with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Core Modules and the fs Mental Model
points: Core modules ship with Node and need no install; import with the node: prefix (import fs from 'node:fs') to make clear they are built in
fs has three API styles for the same operations: callback (fs.readFile(path, cb)), sync (fs.readFileSync) and promise (fs/promises or fs.promises.readFile)
Callback and promise versions run on the libuv thread pool and do not block the event loop; the callback receives (err, data) and err is always the first argument
Sync versions block the whole event loop until finished and throw errors, so wrap them in try/catch
Without an encoding argument readFile returns a Buffer; pass 'utf8' to get a string

chapters.title: fs Workflow: Promises, Callbacks and Sync Compared
points: Preferred style: import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises', then use await inside try/catch
Comparison: callbacks suit legacy code, sync suits startup scripts and CLIs, promises suit servers and everything else
Example: const text = await readFile('a.txt', 'utf8'); await writeFile('b.txt', text.toUpperCase())
writeFile overwrites the file, appendFile adds to it; the flag 'wx' fails if the file already exists
Everyday calls: mkdir(dir, { recursive: true }), readdir, stat, rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true }), access
Mistake: using readFileSync inside a request handler blocks every other request
Mistake: forgetting await or the err check, which causes silent failures and unhandled rejections

chapters.title: path and __dirname in ES Modules
points: path.join(a, b) only concatenates segments and normalizes separators and '..'; the result can stay relative
path.resolve(a, b) builds an absolute path: it processes right to left until the path is absolute, and falls back to process.cwd()
Comparison: path.join('/a', '/b') gives '/a/b' while path.resolve('/a', '/b') gives '/b' because an absolute segment resets the path
__dirname and __filename do not exist in ES modules (type: module or .mjs); they exist only in CommonJS
ESM fix: const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); newer Node also offers import.meta.dirname and import.meta.filename
Mistake: relative paths like './data.json' resolve against process.cwd(), not the file's location, so anchor them with path.join(__dirname, 'data.json')
Helpers: path.basename, path.extname, path.dirname, path.parse; use path.sep and never hard-code '/' or '\\'

chapters.title: The http Module and a Minimal Server
points: http.createServer((req, res) => {...}) returns a server; it runs the callback once per request, and server.listen(port) starts it
req is a readable stream carrying req.method, req.url and req.headers; res is a writable stream
Minimal server: createServer((req, res) => { res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true })) }).listen(3000)
Manual routing with if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/health'); Express and Fastify wrap this same API
The request body arrives in chunks: collect them with req.on('data') and parse JSON in req.on('end') (or use for await (const c of req))
Mistake: forgetting res.end() leaves the request hanging; calling writeHead or setHeader after the body has been sent throws ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT
Mistake: not setting Content-Type, or sending an object instead of a string or Buffer to res.end

chapters.title: os, process, URL and querystring
points: os module: os.cpus().length, os.totalmem(), os.freemem(), os.platform(), os.homedir(), os.tmpdir(), os.EOL

process: process.argv (the first two entries are node and the script path, so use argv.slice(2)), process.env.NAME, process.cwd(), process.pid, process.exit(code), process.memoryUsage(), process.uptime()
process.env values are always strings (PORT='3000'), so convert them with Number() and give defaults with ??
WHATWG URL: const u = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost'); u.pathname; u.searchParams.get('id') (returns null when missing); URLSearchParams supports append, has and toString
Legacy querystring.parse and url.parse are older APIs; prefer URL and URLSearchParams for new code
Mistake: new URL('/path') throws because it needs a base; searchParams values are strings, so cast them
Mistake: using process.exit() instead of letting pending I/O finish; set process.exitCode instead

chapters.title: Node Core Modules Cheat Sheet
points: fs: use promises for servers, sync only at startup, always pass 'utf8', mkdir with recursive: true, and rm with force: true
path: join concatenates, resolve gives an absolute path from cwd, and the ESM __dirname is dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
http: createServer(handler).listen(port); always call res.end(); send a status code and Content-Type via writeHead
process: argv.slice(2) for arguments, env values are strings, and set exitCode instead of calling exit
URL: new URL(req.url, base), then searchParams.get(); querystring and url.parse are legacy
Interview Point: sync vs async fs and the event loop; join vs resolve; why __dirname is missing in ESM; how to read a request body in the raw http module
